report.source_text: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbosacral spine revealed a lobulated homogenously enhancing exophytic lesion involving the conus medullaris and filum terminale (Figure 1). The lesion, measuring 13 × 14 × 22 mm3 and located at the level of the L1/2 lamina was associated with cord edema extending to the level of T11. A further small lesion of 5 mm was also noted in the cauda equina at the L5/S1 level.

report.source_text: Histology demonstrated features of classic HL involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles. The tumor tissue was composed of scattered Hodgkin cells, Reed–Sternberg cells and lacunar cells surrounded by a mix of small lymphocytes, histiocytes, eosinophils and occasional neutrophils (Figure 2). No prominent fibrous bands were present and, therefore, the mixed cellularity subtype was favored. On immunohistochemistry, the tumor cells showed membrane staining for CD30. They showed weak-positive staining for CD20 and PAX5 and were also positive for MUM1 and EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) in-situ hybridization (ISH; Figure 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: classic HL involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old female presented with lower back pain, right L5-S1 radiculopathy, perianal paresthesia, and sphincter dysfunction. MRI lumbar spine with contrast revealed a lobulated enhancing lesion at the conus medullaris and a smaller lesion in the cauda equina. Biopsy of the conus medullaris lesion confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma with characteristic Reed-Sternberg cells and typical immunohistochemical markers including CD30, weak CD20/PAX5, MUM1, and EBER positivity. No CSF analysis results were available. No additional testing or follow-up was documented.
